Definition: Akbor, the name of an Idumaean and of two Israelites
BiblicalUsage: Three men share the name: the father of Baal-hanan, a king of Edom, in Genesis 36; Josiah's courtier, the son of Michaiah, sent to inquire of Huldah the prophetess; and the father of Elnathan, whom Jehoiakim sent to fetch the prophet Uriah from Egypt to kill him. The three men are told apart by their errands — this study covers only how the name is used.
TheologicalSignificance: A shared name carries no lesson of its own. What it shows is the Bible's honesty with ordinary people: one Akbor serves a reforming king, another's son serves a murdering one, and the name is remembered in both stories because God records the servants as well as the kings.
